sentences.text: Through this part, higher capital gains lower a typical person's the predicted chance of an income of $50,000 or less slowly at first, then faster, falling faster once the gain rises above about 3511 US dollars: from about 61% at 0 to about 10% at 6849 US dollars, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted chance cannot go much lower.
For people born in Italy capital gains barely change it, again slowly at first, then faster: from about 61% to about 58%.

This part adds up most characteristics, each on its own: a higher education level lowers a typical person's the predicted chance of an income of $50,000 or less steadily, from about 80% at 7 to about 38% at 13 on the 1-16 scale, as do higher capital losses (about 61% at 0 to about 31% at 1887 US dollars), longer working hours (about 71% at 24 to about 50% at 55 hours a week) and older age (about 69% at 22 to about 47% at 58 years).

Being never married rather than married to a civilian raises it to about 96%, and other marital statuses to about 94%; being a wife rather than a husband lowers it to about 33% and not living in a family to about 48%, while being a woman raises it to about 76%.

Compared with a professional job, farming or fishing raises it to about 87% and other service work to about 86%, while a missing occupation lowers it to about 24%; compared with private work, a missing work class raises it to about 96% and never having worked to above 99% (the model has little data on this, n = 9).

Being born in Colombia raises it to about 99%, in Peru to about 82% and in Mexico to about 76%, while being born in Ireland lowers it to about 34%; a highest education of 1st-4th grade lowers it to about 39%.
Through this part, being born in Laos raises a typical person's the predicted chance of an income of $50,000 or less from about 61% to above 99% (the model has little data on this, n = 17).
Through this part, a protective-service job lowers a typical person's the predicted chance of an income of $50,000 or less from about 61% to about 48%.
Through this part, being born in Portugal lowers a typical person's the predicted chance of an income of $50,000 or less from about 61% to about 38%.
Through this part, being born in Poland raises a typical person's the predicted chance of an income of $50,000 or less from about 61% to about 66%.
This part, built around a marital status of married with the spouse absent, barely changes the predictions (about 61% to about 59%).
Through this part, an armed-forces job lowers a typical person's the predicted chance of an income of $50,000 or less from about 61% to about 52% (the model has little data on this, n = 12).
Through this part, being born in India raises a typical person's the predicted chance of an income of $50,000 or less a little, from about 61% to about 63%.

parts.name: capital_gain_core
parts.original_hypothesis: Rectified multi-stage pipeline transforming capital-gain (-63). Capital-gain fans through a depth-3 ReLU cascade (3446->4739->2129 plus direct) converging on hub 655, read out to the output via four opposing-sign weights (655/313 vs 5102/6421). Over the observed range of capital-gain the seven neurons collapse to a SINGLE-KNOT threshold - flat for the ~90% with zero capital-gain, one knot, then a linear ramp - i.e. functionally a single ReLU (see Figure: capgain transfer curve, constant slope after one knot across the full data range). The cascade's earlier inner knots (z~-0.42, z~-0.03) fall below the data floor or are masked by the output unit's clipping, and the four readouts all bend at the same threshold, so they set slope and offset but add NO further knots. The depth-3 structure therefore exceeds the single threshold it produces over the data - excess structure, the same phenomenon as the fused native-country terms below. (Claim bounded to the observed data range; depth may act on out-of-range capital-gain.) Also absorbs native-country one-hots -73/-81/-82/-89/-94, which carry large weights but are shown inert by ablation (test AUC 0.9055->0.9054 on the full split; memorisation on tiny support).
